workItems.title: Close critical remote-administration and runtime security paths
workItems.rationale: Dedicated-server chat no longer dispatches RCON: messages are broadcast only, and rconPassword/rconPort are reserved and inactive. A direct slash-chat regression proves that boundary, while RemoteDebug unit tests cover loopback authorization. 2026-09-12 progress: built-in RemoteDebug command types are now reserved against public handler rebinding, with a hostile probe and RemoteAdmin regression proving a replacement cannot downgrade authorization. 2026-09-13 progress: the local area-control HMAC replay ledger now fails closed at the existing 4,096-entry bound on Windows and POSIX, with a capacity regression. 2026-09-14 progress: the Multiplayer Quick Start now labels administration as trusted local-only, removes the sample password, and states that remote RCON is unavailable. 2026-09-14 additional progress: stale Memory Integrity documentation now names the trusted local administration boundary and is protected by a site-contract regression against chat/remote RCON wording. 2026-09-24 progress: gateway area-control writes one bounded, secret-free audit record per frame (reason, phase, epoch, sanitized session prefix, outcome) with per-reason counters, SparkServer now initializes Spark::Logger with a stderr sink at Start() so those records leave the process (SparkServerApplication_StartInstallsLogSinkWhenHostHasNone), and live loopback regressions prove wrong-key MAC, stale/future timestamp and replayed-nonce frames are rejected before the epoch fence; ExecuteRcon audits handler exceptions as disposition=failed without exception text, GetRconCommands returns a locked snapshot, and the inactive rconPassword is securely cleared at startup; RemoteAdmin_ExpiredDenied exercises a bounded loopback lifetime and RemoteDebug counts audit-ring evictions; SECURITY.md now lists remote-administration trust boundaries and audit record formats with the security owner and reviewer explicitly unassigned. 2026-09-24 OD-05 progress: the owner decided remote administration stays permanently unavailable in stable-v1 and no authenticated remote-admin channel is built. Every remote entry point is now compiled out rather than reserved: ServerConfig no longer has rconPassword/rconPort, RemoteDebugSystem no longer has StartServer(port)/ConnectToTarget, RemoteDebugClient no longer has Connect(address, port), and RemoteDebugServer::StartListening() takes no port, so no config value or CLI switch can enable remote administration. Tests/TestSEC100RemoteAdminUnavailableReal.cpp holds this with compile-time requires-expression checks on those named entry points and on the ServerConfig field names rconPassword/rconPort/enableRcon/enableRemoteAdministration (verified to fail all six against the prior headers; a differently named field would not be detected) plus runtime selectors proving a raw principal-less queue call is denied and audited as AnonymousDenied and the only local grant cannot reach console_cmd/property_set (AuthorizationDenied); the ENABLE_NETWORKING=OFF contract fixture now fails to compile if DedicatedServer or ServerConfig is declared in a networking-off configuration; it is a local compile contract only, because no hosted CI lane configures a networking-off tree with tests enabled. Gateway area control is same-user SparkServer/SparkGateway IPC, not remote administration, and neither process ships in stable-v1. SECURITY.md, the wiki and site-data label remote administration unavailable. These are local results only. SEC-100 remains open because the reviewed threat model with a named security owner and reviewer, and exact-SHA hosted security-runtime/network-integration evidence, are still absent.
implementationScope: Disable chat-triggered RCON immediately
Keep remote administration permanently unavailable in stable-v1 (OD-05): no remote-admin channel, entry point, or enabling config/CLI switch
Validate tokens/secrets in constant time
Add roles, least privilege, expiry, replay protection, rate limits, and audit logs
Separate local console and remotely invocable command registries
Document the threat model and security owner
acceptanceCriteria: Anonymous and normal clients cannot invoke any administrative command
Invalid, expired, replayed, downgraded, or rate-limited credentials fail closed
Every attempt is auditable without logging reusable secrets
Remote administration is permanently unavailable in stable-v1 and no configuration or command-line switch enables it (OD-05)
performanceBudgets: Admin authentication does not block the simulation thread
websiteImpact: The site must label remote administration unsafe/unavailable until this item closes
risks: Retaining a compatibility backdoor to the old chat command
outOfScope: Building a full hosted operator dashboard
definitionOfDone: Threat model and audit format are reviewed

workItems.title: Establish software supply-chain and dependency policy
workItems.rationale: Workflow actions use mutable major tags, dependency inventories disagree, CodeQL builds only part of the product, and releases lack SBOM/provenance/security gates. 2026-09-12 progress: the release prepare job now runs the existing fail-closed supply-chain checker, including dependency, vendored-content, and action-pin policy, before computing release metadata. 2026-09-13 progress: the supply-chain lock now requires a bounded, case-insensitive-unique, non-waiving exception schema with named owners, valid expiries, adversarial tests, and required legal-compliance CI wiring. Publisher identity, signed-artifact success evidence, consumer verification, vulnerability/license/secret scan policy, and protected release approval remain open. 2026-09-24 progress: tools/generate-sbom.py generates a deterministic, --check-reproducible SPDX 2.3 SBOM from dependencies.lock and supply-chain.lock (license_policy SPDX, gitlinks, vendored tree digests), bound to the source SHA and the committed dependency-lock digest that REL-100 provenance records; its reconcile mode classifies an install manifest or staged package with the GOV-400 package rule set and fails on unmapped or unlocked third-party payload, a locked shipped dependency that is absent, or a notice inventory from a different lock. A local Linux GCC Release install (2515 files) reconciles; Windows and hosted package reconciliation evidence and release.yml wiring remain open. 2026-09-25 progress: tools/check-secret-scan.py scans every git-tracked regular file with the OPS-100 secret_policy detectors and fails on any finding not covered by an exact, owned, unexpired <rule>:<path> exception that reuses the supply-chain exception schema plus a required reviewed finding count (a new finding in an excepted file fails; a lower count must be ratcheted down); the new required secret-scan job in build.yml runs it with its adversarial tests. The gate narrows the structured-credential lexer (credential-naming last key segment, :: scope operators and $VAR/${..}/%s-style references excluded, quoted literals only in programming-language source while scripts, Dockerfiles, dotfile/suffixless credential stores, Markdown and configs also flag unquoted values) and applies only the PEM and self-identifying token detectors to NUL-containing binary files; SECURITY.md documents the narrowing. Hosted exact-SHA evidence for the job is still open.
implementationScope: Pin actions to commit SHAs
Make dependencies.lock authoritative and generate other inventories
Add vulnerability, license, secret, and artifact malware gates
Expand CodeQL across all shipped products and website scripts
Define severity exceptions with owner and expiry
Feed SBOM/provenance into release
acceptanceCriteria: No unpinned action or unmanaged dependency remains
Critical/high findings block without an owned expiring exception
Final package inventory reconciles with source lock
Release artifacts include verifiable supply-chain evidence
performanceBudgets: Security scans complete inside merge/release SLAs
websiteImpact: Security and supply-chain language links to exact passing evidence
risks: Scanner noise leading to blanket exclusions
evidence: ThirdParty/supply-chain.lock — authoritative full tracked-payload lock with tree digests, sentinel records, action pins, and submodule identities
tools/check-supply-chain.py — bounded, fail-closed verifier using Git-index inventory and structured YAML action parsing
.github/workflows/build.yml — check-supply-chain is required by both gate jobs
tools/generate-sbom.py — lock-derived SPDX 2.3 SBOM (source-SHA and dependency-lock digest bound, --check reproducible) and package-inventory reconciliation over the GOV-400 package rule set
Tests/Tools/test_generate_sbom.py — forged, unlocked, missing, stale-declaration, and wrong-lock notice cases (ctest SupplyChain_SbomAndPackageReconciliation; build.yml check-supply-chain job)

tools/check-secret-scan.py — bounded git-index secret scan with the OPS-100 tools/ops/secret_policy.py detectors (no symlink following, oversize files fail, values never printed); exceptions in tools/secret-scan-exceptions.json reuse the supply-chain validate_exception_records schema with exact <rule>:<path> scopes, a 366-day expiry horizon, and stale-exception failure; local run 2026-09-25: 6160 files scanned, 0 unexcepted findings, 20 owned fixture exceptions

Tests/Tools/test_check_secret_scan.py — planted tokens/PEM/credentials, symlink, oversize, expired, stale, wildcard, directory-scoped, duplicate-id and schema-invalid exception cases (ctest SecretScan_RepositoryGate; required build.yml secret-scan job)

Release wiring of lock-derived SBOM and package reconciliation (release.yml package jobs) with hosted Windows and Linux package evidence

workItems.title: Fuzz and bound every stable-v1 untrusted file and package parser
workItems.rationale: Saves, scenes, assets, shaders, archives, manifests, and crash metadata cross stable-v1 trust boundaries without a unified fuzz/bounds gate; packet and script campaigns belong to the excluded networking and scripting surfaces. 2026-09-05 progress (partial hardening, no fuzz harness): Json::ParseBounded/JsonLimits budgets on every default parse entry point; mod.json and mod config capped at 64 KB / depth 16 / 4096 nodes and parsed strictly; scene manifests capped at 8 MB / 100,000 entries with path containment; .spk decompression ratio bounded at Open; .skel/.sanim name-length and parentIndex validation; Spark::IsVirtualPathSafe. Tests/TestSecurityParsersReal.cpp now executes the shipped parsers (the packet-validator evidence is tracked under NET-100). 2026-09-12 progress: SparkPak now rejects unsafe traversal entry names while opening the archive, with a production regression fixture. 2026-09-13 additional progress: installer state manifests now reject inputs above 64 KiB and detect shrink/growth races while reading, with focused native install-state coverage. 2026-09-14 progress: the first production-entry-point Clang/libFuzzer target exercises Spark::Json::ParseBounded with a bounded seven-seed corpus, explicit 4 KiB/32-level/256 MiB/1-second limits, a 4-second active smoke, and a 10-second CTest bound. 2026-09-20 progress: the production .nnw loader now validates bounded dimensions, connectivity, activation/optimizer values, checked parameter counts, exact payload size, and saver symmetry before allocating weight/optimizer payloads; a direct LoadWeights libFuzzer target is bound to an eight-seed corpus. 2026-09-21 progress: the production crash-manifest parser now has a direct bounded Clang/libFuzzer target and six-seed corpus. Its seed bytes are LF-pinned and independently verified in a fresh Windows-style autocrlf checkout. 2026-09-24 OD-21 triage: all 149 deferred parser candidates were classified per file by reading the code; 28 became new blocked parser boundaries (untrusted-file, untrusted-network, or untrusted-ipc, including the collaborative-edit TCP codec, editor/engine named pipe, LAN discovery beacons, game-module save-state decoders, and two tinyobj OBJ loaders), 3 joined existing blocked records, and 115 received OD-21 exemptions (68 delegating-call-site, 29 not-a-parser, 10 helper, 6 same-process-data, 2 developer-tooling) that the fuzz-policy gate now schema-checks, ties to inventoried parsers, and invalidates when a file's detector hits change. 2026-09-25 progress: the production SceneManifest::ParseFromString (.sparkscene) parser has a direct Clang/libFuzzer + ASan/UBSan target (SparkFuzzSceneManifest / FuzzSceneManifestSmoke) that aborts on any accepted path that climbs out of the root under Windows separator semantics (an independent lexical walk in the adapter, not the parser's own filter), contains a control byte, or fails IsVirtualPathSafe, or on exceeding the entry cap, with an eight-seed deterministic -runs replay corpus (valid, traversal, reserved device names, high entry count, deep path nesting, CRLF/comments, duplicate/unknown keys, binary noise); the 8 MB and 100,000-entry caps sit above the smoke's max_len and are pinned by SceneManifest_EntryCapKeepsExactlyTheLimit and SceneManifest_ByteCapRejectsOversizedContent. Spark::IsVirtualPathSafe now treats a backslash as a separator on every host and rejects control bytes, so a Linux-validated manifest can no longer carry '..\..\x' (which POSIX normalizes to one harmless component) or a NUL-truncated path to Windows (SceneManifest_ParseDropsBackslashTraversalOnEveryHost, SceneManifest_ParseDropsControlBytePaths). Exemption ledger since the 2026-09-24 triage (115): the RHI-210 golden-image commit replaced the GoldenImageTest.h developer-tooling exemption with GoldenImagePng.h and GoldenImageManifest.h (net +1, 116), and two new /proc/self readers (SparkEngineLinuxHeadless.cpp, ServerHealth.cpp) received not-a-parser exemptions (118). The structural policy gate records 5 fuzzed parsers, 5 corpora, 130 blocked parser targets, 0 deferred candidates, and 118 exemptions; the exemptions are recorded judgement awaiting independent security review, and exact-SHA hosted sanitizer evidence, runtime coverage, the 130 missing harnesses, and scheduled campaigns remain open. 2026-09-25 progress: a non-blocking nightly/workflow_dispatch `fuzz-scheduled` job (.github/workflows/fuzz-scheduled.yml) runs tools/fuzz-policy/run_campaign.py, which discovers every ctest `fuzz`-labelled target, mutates a disposable copy of its committed corpus for a per-target budget under the smoke's own limits (with UBSAN_OPTIONS halt_on_error=1 so SparkFuzzJsonUtils' recoverable UBSan checks also abort, plus a log scan for any 'runtime error:' report), minimizes every crash/leak/timeout/OOM reproducer with -minimize_crash, retains raw and minimized files plus per-target duration/executions/crash-free time in an uploaded artifact whose summary is rewritten after every target, exits 1 on any finding and 2 on a setup error, refuses budgets that exceed the job timeout, and fails if a committed corpus changes (Tests/fuzz-policy/test_fuzz_campaign.py, run by FuzzPolicyAdversarial); no hosted campaign run is recorded yet, so this adds workflow capability, not campaign evidence. Do not promote SEC-120 or parser coverage from these structural slices alone.
implementationScope: Create libFuzzer/AFL-compatible targets and seed corpora for save, scene, asset, shader, archive, manifest, and crash inputs
Set file, allocation, depth, and time limits
Run ASan/UBSan fuzz smoke on every change and longer scheduled campaigns
Persist minimized regressions as tests
acceptanceCriteria: Malformed input cannot cause crash, OOB, path escape, integer overflow, or unbounded allocation/time
Every found issue lands with a minimized regression fixture
Required fuzz smoke is deterministic and blocking
websiteImpact: Parser/protocol safety claims require current fuzz evidence
risks: Fuzz harnesses bypassing production entry points
outOfScope: AngelScript and visual-script fuzzing behind G11
definitionOfDone: Budgets and regression workflow are enforced
Remaining: production harnesses for 102 blocked parsers, classification of 151 deferred candidates, retained exact-SHA sanitizer evidence, minimized regression fixtures, and scheduled campaigns

workItems.title: Replace placeholder transport security with audited authenticated encryption
workItems.rationale: MMOFPS authentication fields can carry plaintext credentials, while engine networking includes XOR/MT19937/FNV placeholder security that cannot support a secure-networking claim. 2026-09-05 progress (no promotion): PacketValidator string screening is now enforced through schema-declared stringFieldOffset/NO_STRING_FIELDS (the sanitizeStrings flag was removed), ChatMessage is one NetBuffer string at offset 0, UTF-8 text is accepted, and the packet.stats string counter is a real count; Tests/TestPacketValidator.cpp and Tests/TestPacketValidatorReal.cpp execute the shipped validator. The transport still carries the XOR/MT19937/FNV placeholder security, so no secure-networking claim changes.
implementationScope: Adopt maintained DTLS/TLS or reviewed AEAD handshake/library
Use CSPRNG keys/nonces and authenticated sessions
Add replay windows, key rotation, downgrade protection, packet bounds, and protocol negotiation
Remove or isolate placeholder crypto
Redact credentials from logs/crash data
Obtain independent security review
Fuzz packet framing, negotiation, replay windows, and malformed encrypted traffic through the production transport
acceptanceCriteria: Packet capture contains no reusable credential or plaintext authentication data
Tamper, replay, nonce reuse, wrong key, truncation, reorder, downgrade, and malformed handshake fail closed
Authentication and gameplay share the production encrypted path
No custom cryptographic primitive remains in the advertised transport
commands: rg -n "mt19937|FNV|XOR|placeholder for DTLS|placeholder for AES|char pass" SparkEngine/Source GameModules/SparkGameMMOFPS
performanceBudgets: Encryption overhead fits the declared server tick and bandwidth budgets

workItems.title: Define and implement the production online-service boundary
workItems.rationale: Engine networking and reference modules do not provide turnkey identity, matchmaking, fleet, secrets, abuse, moderation, entitlement, billing, or incident control-plane services. Owner decision OD-08 (2026-09-24, docs/readiness/OWNER-DECISIONS.md): identity, matchmaking, fleet, entitlement and billing services are out of engine scope; the engine ships no hosted online services. This item owns documenting that service boundary. 2026-09-24 progress: wiki/advanced/Online-Service-Boundary.md (in wiki/_Sidebar.md) is the service-boundary contract: it lists what the engine provides (UDP transport, the IGatewayAuthenticator/KeyFileAuthenticator admission hook, sensitive-handler and PBKDF2 helpers, the SparkServer/SparkGateway/SparkDaemon/SparkCollabServer processes, and the IOnlinePlatform interface with its in-memory NullOnlinePlatform and compile-only platform stubs), what it does not provide (identity, matchmaking, fleet, entitlement, billing, hosted player data, operations), and the trust boundaries between them. wiki/gameplay-tools/Online-Services.md no longer claims nonexistent ENABLE_STEAM/ENABLE_EOS options or local-storage cloud saves. tools/site-data/validate.py now rejects (hosted_online_service_claim_errors) any non-negated claim of hosted, managed, or turnkey online services on every governed public claim surface, the two online-service pages, and docs/site/readiness.json; Tests/Tools/test_site_data_contract.py OnlineServiceBoundaryTests covers claims, negations, cross-sentence negation, and the live repository surfaces. 2026-09-25 progress: docs/specs/online-services.md (contract version 1.0) is the boundary specification. It separates the engine SDK interfaces (IOnlinePlatform/OnlineServiceManager, NetworkManager, DedicatedServer, SparkServer, the SparkGateway admission and area-control plane, SparkDaemon) from product-owned identity, matchmaking, fleet, moderation, entitlement, billing, player-data and operations services, and draws them in a Mermaid deployment diagram. It names trust boundaries B1-B9, gives per-call timeout/retry/circuit-breaker budgets and failure semantics, and labels every shipped adapter local/deterministic, local reference, or stub, never production. The spec states which budgets the code does not enforce yet (the IOnlinePlatform game-thread limit and circuit breaker). It is a governed surface of validate_online_service_boundary (ONLINE_SERVICE_BOUNDARY_SURFACES) and was removed from FUTURE_ACCEPTANCE_PATHS. Still open: enforcement of the IOnlinePlatform budgets in OnlineServiceManager, deterministic local adapters with the OnlineServices_Contract/OnlineServices_Degraded/SessionCompatibility_* tests under the online-services ctest label, safe and observable failure of production adapters, and the service-contract and network-integration CI jobs.

workItems.title: Make multiplayer persistence transactional, migratable, backed up, and recoverable
workItems.rationale: MMO/MMOFPS reference persistence is local/demo-grade and does not prove atomic ownership, schema migration, concurrent writes, backups, restore, or disaster recovery. 2026-09-05 progress: AsyncDatabase's key-value store no longer truncates the live file on every write, so the interrupted-write acceptance now also covers that store (Tests/TestSaveSystemRoundTripReal.cpp, AsyncDatabaseReal_*); MMO/MMOFPS module persistence is unchanged and the item stays open. 2026-09-13 progress: AsyncDatabase now explicitly durably flushes its completed sibling revision before atomic replacement on Windows and POSIX, with a production round-trip regression and a source policy contract; concurrent module writes, migrations, backup/restore, and disaster-recovery evidence remain open. 2026-09-24 progress (OD-22): Tests/TestDATA120SecretsAtRest.cpp (Persistence_Secrets_*) drives the production TERRAFRONT account store (TFAccountSystem over TFDatabase) and the MMO AsyncDatabase key-value store (MMOPersistenceSystem) against real files, with a structural guard for the MMO account system (it has no persistence path; the written store holds no password, hash, or token and a restarted account system rejects the old token), and scans the shipped config trees (SparkEngine/Resources/Config, the runtime Assets directories, and the SparkServer/SparkGateway operator example configs), asserting that only salted PBKDF2 hashes are persisted (account-row column allowlist, distinct salts, restart re-login from the hash), that no plaintext or hex-encoded password or session token reaches either store, and that no credential-shaped key or user:password@ URL appears in shipped config; no violation was found, so no production fix was needed. Host full-disk encryption is documented as the operator responsibility in wiki/gameplay-tools/Persistence-System.md and SECURITY.md. This covers the secrets half of the encrypt-and-separate-secrets scope only; the transactional, migration, backup/restore, and recovery acceptance criteria remain open.

Version schemas and migrations
Enforce ownership and optimistic/concurrency controls

workItems.title: Secure and complete crash reporting, telemetry delivery, and symbol operations
workItems.rationale: Crash manifests are now transport-free, pinned to a private artifact root, and handled by a read-only external reporter; C++ telemetry has bounded durable spool/retry/drop accounting. 2026-09-12 progress (superseded 2026-09-24): crash-upload proxy and FTP endpoint logs were reduced to scheme and host; that uploader code and its endpoint-redaction regressions were deleted with the in-process uploader below. 2026-09-13 progress: CrashHandler no longer invokes the legacy in-process uploader or archive/consent fallback; it always publishes a local manifest and launches the read-only reporter for interactive processes, with a source-policy regression. 2026-09-24 progress (local only): the unreferenced in-process CrashReportUploader (GitHub PAT/SMTP/FTP/Dropbox/HTTP/proxy transport) was deleted; CrashConfig, [CrashReporting] settings and SetupCrashHandler no longer carry or read any upload URL, relay URL, GitHub token or SMTP credential; EngineSettings::Load drops the retired keys from settings.ini/settings.local.ini so Save() cannot write them back; both shipped settings.ini files no longer contain them; the uploader-only ComputeStackHash dedup parser was deleted with it, since nothing else called it; SparkCrashReporter.ManifestCompatibility now carries the crash-security label. 2026-09-25 progress (local only): the production crash-capture producer test now also runs on POSIX, where the ungated assertion report is log-only with an empty dumpFile, and CrashCapturePackageSecurity is registered on native Linux/macOS hosts that build SparkCrashReporter; ctest -L crash-security passes 4/4 on Linux. The POSIX report still carries unredacted absolute module paths and no module build-id. OPS-100 remains open because controlled relay delivery, scoped authorization, release symbolication, privacy/retention review, and exact-SHA crash evidence are absent.
implementationScope: Remove reusable credentials from manifests/client configuration
Use controlled relay and scoped ephemeral authorization
Restrict crash directories and canonicalize/allowlist all file paths
Add redaction, consent, retention, size, and deletion policy
Implement truthful queued/delivered/rejected/failed states
Publish private symbols indexed by build ID and verify symbolication
Add durable telemetry spool/retry/drop accounting
acceptanceCriteria: Crash artifacts contain no reusable secret
Malicious manifest/symlink/path input cannot read or delete outside owned crash data
Declined consent transmits nothing
A synthetic release crash reaches the test relay and symbolicates to source
Endpoint outage recovers within documented spool/drop bounds
performanceBudgets: Crash handling is bounded and avoids deadlock/allocation in compromised process context

definitionOfDone: Privacy/retention policy and runbook are reviewed

evidence.scope: Local C++ runtime, offline adversarial-validation, and configured CI-lane evidence only. The reporter rejects transport fields and is intentionally read-only; local telemetry has bounded spool/retry/drop accounting. This is not runtime-delivery evidence, controlled-relay delivery, privacy/retention review, private-symbol publication, release-canary symbolication, or exact-SHA hosted evidence.
tooling: tools/ops/secret_policy.py: JSON-aware recursive redaction (structural parse, redact sensitive values at any depth/type, re-serialize valid JSON); bounded linear lexer for generic-text credentials (multiword/quoted/escaped, per-line/document/secret ceilings); single-pass bounded PEM parser for RSA/EC/DSA/OPENSSH/ENCRYPTED/generic PRIVATE KEY families with label matching; location sanitization via keyed hashes to suppress secret-bearing paths; archive detection by ZIP magic bytes (not suffix) with minidump structure validation; explicit size/depth/count ceilings throughout
tools/ops/validate_crash_package.py validates strict bounded manifests and referenced artifacts through a pinned authoritative root without modifying them
tools/ops/validate_telemetry_spool.py validates all spool entries, strict event JSON, timestamps, names, retention observations, and offline resource bounds

tools/ops/redact_secrets.py applies the shared bounded secret policy, scans directories with post-scan re-enumeration and identity comparison to detect concurrent additions/replacements, and only redacts to stdout
tests: Tests/Tools/test_ops100_crash_security.py covers cross-platform path spellings, junction/hardlink rejection, referenced artifacts, strict JSON, opaque binaries, and archive policy
Tests/Tools/test_ops100_telemetry_spool.py covers unmatched-file accounting, hardlinks/junctions, dual retention clocks, strict schema/types, and reusable secrets
Tests/Tools/test_ops100_redaction.py covers credential families, binary/ZIP handling, missing and unreadable inputs, stdout-only redaction, and performance regression

Tests/Tools/test_ops100_adversarial.py covers: (1) JSON structural parse/recursive redact with nested/brace/escaped/empty/oversized/adjacent-safe/malformed inputs; (2) bounded linear lexer with multiword/quoted/escaped/comma/semicolon/brace/oversized/backtracking/ceiling tests; (3) location safety with keyed-hash suppression of secret-bearing paths; (4) PEM single-pass parser for RSA/EC/DSA/OPENSSH/ENCRYPTED/generic/mismatched/unmatched/32MB-linear inputs; (5) archive magic detection for renamed ZIP, minidump validation, nested archive by magic; (6) scan race detection for concurrent addition/replacement, symlink/hardlink rejection; (7) CI gate registration with path coverage and required-gate inclusion; (8) docs/evidence accuracy with honest scope and open status

SparkCrashReporter/tests/CrashReporterManifestTests.cpp, exercised by SparkCrashReporter.ManifestCompatibility, proves transport fields are discarded, manifests omit them, the reporter is truthful and read-only, and path/identity/size/consent defenses reject hostile artifacts

Tests/TestEngineSettingsReal.cpp CrashSettings_RetiredTransportCredentialsAreDroppedOnLoadAndNeverWritten (ctest CrashSettingsCredentials, label crash-security) proves retired crash-transport keys from settings.ini and settings.local.ini are dropped on load and never saved; Tests/Tools/test_ops100_crash_security.py source/settings policy checks forbid credential-bearing crash configuration, environment overrides, and transport calls in SparkEngine/Source and shipped settings

Tests/TestTelemetrySpool.cpp, exercised by TelemetrySpool, proves C++ durable spool recovery, terminal rejection, retry boundaries, bounds/drop accounting, consent revocation, and hostile artifact rejection

Tests/Tools/run_crash_capture_security.py, registered as ctest CrashCapturePackageSecurity (labels crash-security;security;integration) on every native host that builds SparkCrashReporter with miniz (stub builds and cross-compiles are excluded), runs the production producer test CrashHandler_UngatedReportWritesAnArtifactAndTheAssertGateDoesNot (Tests/TestCrashHandlerGatingReal.cpp, Windows minidump path and POSIX log-only assertion path) in an isolated temporary root and validates its untouched artifacts with the native reporter and validate_crash_package.py, including traversal and legacy-transport-field copies; on POSIX the owned work root is removed through a directory fd pinned to its recorded identity (Windows retains it); 2026-09-25 local Linux run (linux-gcc-release): ctest -L crash-security passes. The Linux Shipping configuration (MinSizeRel, SPARK_SHIPPING) was not run locally and is unverified. No hosted record.

workItems.title: Add production server observability, load, soak, backup, and incident gates
workItems.rationale: Profiling utilities and local chaos scripts do not substitute for externally consumable health/readiness, SLOs, alerts, long soaks, backup/restore, and incident response evidence.
implementationScope: Expose structured logs, metrics, health, readiness, and build/version identity
Define frame/tick/network/persistence/error SLOs and alerts
Run multi-process loss/latency/load/chaos/soak scenarios
